tags: why do dogs chase their tails
script: Few things are funnier than a dog spinning in circles after its own tail. For puppies, it's often simple play and exploration, because they're still discovering their own bodies and may genuinely not realize the tail belongs to them. Chasing is also built into a dog's instincts, so a moving object right behind them is hard to resist. Adult dogs may do it when they're bored, excited, or have extra energy, and a few spins can be a cheerful way to burn it off. Sometimes, though, tail chasing has a physical reason, like an itch, irritation, fleas, or discomfort around the tail or anal glands, and then it's worth checking with your vet. Persistent, intense spinning that's hard to interrupt can also be linked to anxiety or compulsive behavior, particularly in some breeds. To keep it healthy, make sure your dog gets enough exercise, puzzle toys and mental work every day. If you notice your dog chasing for long stretches, hurting the tail, or ignoring you completely, get professional advice. Occasional spins, on the other hand, are just a goofy part of being a dog.
